items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: Vanessa Rubin, I produced her first album. Her first two albums.

ctx.x: Stuff that I wrote when I was fourteen, fifteen years old, is now being recorded. I present this tune to a person, oh, it’s a great tune. You know Vanessa Williams — Vanessa Williams — Vanessa Rubin, I produced her first album. Her first two albums. And she did a song of mine that I wrote when I was fifteen years old. The lyrics were written much later, but the song itself was written when I was fifteen. I played it for her, she loved it, it got reviewed in a CD magazine, the year-end review of CDs for that year.…

reviewer somehow thought that my tune was a standard. He said well Vanessa recorded the standards, “Got the World on a String,” “Tenderly,” “Autumn” blah-blah. I said “Autumn,” that’s my song. First recording of the song. But he thought it was a standard, which made me feel very good. Because one thing that — you may get disagreement from people — but one thing that bothers me is that a lot of the cats now are not writing the new standards.
